messages:
Logan Wright: quick review on ENG-2841 before we lock it — aggregation latency + DQ risks. goal is: signals land in HubSpot fast enough that SDR outreach isn’t 24h late.

Nadia Rahman: +1. main concern: late-arriving telemetry + billing events. if we do a pure “yesterday rollup once/day” we’ll be wrong for hours, and then backfills will churn the numbers.

Mei Lin: current pipeline reality:
- raw events in lake: near-real-time, but some SDK events show up 10–45m late (mobile + retries)
- billing meter events: more stable but can lag 30–90m around top-of-hour
- error-rate metrics (gateway): fast, but we sometimes drop samples during incident mitigations

Caleb Johnson: and the error-rate signal is super sensitive. if a customer has 3% 5xx for 15 mins we want to catch it same day, not next.

Rafael Mendes: from SRE angle: if this runs every 5 mins and it’s expensive / flaky, oncall will hate it. we need a cadence that’s (a) predictable, (b) easy to backfill, (c) alertable when it stalls.

Allison Grant: + we should define “freshness” and “completeness” separately. dashboards can show freshness, but scoring should avoid acting on incomplete windows.

Logan Wright: proposal I have in mind:
- 7d windows: refresh hourly (top of hour), using watermark w/ 2h delay (only aggregate events older than now-2h)
- 14d + 30d windows: refresh daily (02:00 UTC), with a nightly backfill that reprocesses last 3 days to capture late arrivals
- plus: weekly backfill for last 30d (Sunday 03:00 UTC) for any stragglers / schema fixes

Nadia Rahman: hourly for 7d is fine if we gate scoring on “window is closed enough”. the 2h delay helps. but we should document that “7d spend” is “through now-2h”.

Mei Lin: implementation detail: we can do incremental merges by (account_id, day) partitions. so hourly job only touches “today” + “yesterday” partitions, not the whole 7d.

Mei Lin: something like:
```
MERGE INTO agg_usage_daily d
USING staging s
ON d.account_id = s.account_id AND d.day = s.day
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET ...
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT ...
```
then 7d/14d/30d rollups are derived from daily table.

Caleb Johnson: derived rollups ok. but for error-rate / rate-limit spikes we also need shorter windows (like 1h / 6h) eventually. v1 only 7/14/30 but want to avoid designing ourselves into a corner.

Logan Wright: yes — v1 scope is 7/14/30 for spend/tokens/concurrency + some counts (429s, routing failures). but we can add “recent_1h_429s” later as a separate table.

Rafael Mendes: if hourly rollup depends on daily partitions, that’s still ok. but make sure jobs are idempotent and have a dead-simple re-run story.

Allison Grant: DQ checks I want before we trust this:
1) event volume anomaly detection (per region) — if ingestion drops, we don’t want to trigger “usage down” / “rate-limit up” weirdness
2) “late event rate” metric: % of events arriving >2h late
3) row count + null checks on key fields (account_id, model, tokens)
4) “window completeness” boolean exposed to scoring (e.g., completeness_score >= 0.98)

Nadia Rahman: (4) might be too fancy for v1 but at least a “data_freshness_minutes” and “aggregation_lag_minutes” field will help. scoring can suppress if lag > threshold.

Cole Summers: billing hook note: spend is computed from rated usage, which is more stable but can lag when we do end-of-day adjustments or credit grants. if we’re using spend growth as a trigger, we should be explicit whether it’s “estimated spend” vs “invoiced spend”.

Logan Wright: good call. for signals, we’re using “estimated_usd” from rated usage table (post-discount but pre-invoice adjustments). we’ll include a field name in schema so no one assumes it matches invoices.

Mei Lin: on backfills: nightly “reprocess last 3 days” is cheap. weekly “reprocess last 30 days” is heavier but fine off-peak. if we have a schema change, we can run an ad-hoc backfill with a date range.

Rafael Mendes: please add a runbook section: how to backfill without duplicating downstream events. (idempotency keys + separate “aggregation updated” vs “signal emitted”)

Nadia Rahman: +1. I’m worried about backfill causing the scoring service to think “new data” and emit again. we should ensure scoring reads from a stable snapshot timestamp and dedupes.

Logan Wright: scoring dedupe is in ENG-2842, but we’ll add “source_agg_version” and “window_end_ts” to the payload so idempotency key includes those.

Allison Grant: also define the SLO:
- 7d rollups freshness: p95 < 2.5h
- daily 14/30 refresh completes by 03:30 UTC
- backfill completion metrics emitted to Grafana

Caleb Johnson: what about concurrency? that’s from gateway logs, right? those are pretty real-time.

Mei Lin: concurrency is aggregated from request logs in ClickHouse, then exported. it’s usually <10m, but can lag if we have CH maintenance. I’d treat it like the rest: hourly rollup with watermark.

Cole Summers: one more DQ risk: account mapping changes (domain merges, org_id changes). if we join late, we can mis-attribute usage. do we have a stable account_id at ingest?

Nadia Rahman: we do, but there are occasional backfills when an org is merged. those are rare but we should handle with the weekly 30d backfill.

Logan Wright: ok, let’s lock decisions:
- 7d: hourly refresh, watermark = now-2h, touches today+1 day partitions
- 14d/30d: daily refresh at 02:00 UTC
- Nightly backfill: reprocess last 3 days (covers late arrivals + small fixes)
- Weekly backfill: reprocess last 30 days (Sun 03:00 UTC)
- Scoring suppression: if agg lag > 4h, don’t emit “fresh” signals (log + alert instead)
- DQ: add basic checks (nulls/rowcounts/volume anomaly) + freshness metrics

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: please add alerting thresholds:
- hourly job misses 2 consecutive runs
- daily job not complete by 04:00 UTC
- lag metric > 6h for >30m

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: and make sure dashboards show job runtime + rows processed. helps debug.

Mei Lin: I’ll update ENG-2841 with cadence/backfill details and add the incremental partition approach. also will add a “late_arrival_minutes” metric from ingest_ts - event_ts distribution.

Nadia Rahman: I’ll write up the watermark logic + definitions so product doesn’t interpret numbers as “real-time”.

Logan Wright: great. action items:
- Mei: ticket update + schema fields for freshness/lag (EOD tomorrow)
- Nadia: watermark + semantics doc (tomorrow)
- Rafa/Allison: SLO + alerts list in runbook (by end of week)

Caleb Johnson: can we also add a quick note for PMs: signals based on 7d numbers won’t fire within first 2h of a big spike. that’s acceptable.

Logan Wright: yep. will add to doc + call out “fast pain signals” are v1.1.

Cole Summers: sounds good. ping me if spend numbers look weird after nightly backfill — I can sanity check rated usage.

Logan Wright: thanks all.
